answer: To resist Sybil attacks, each agent must lock a capital bond equal to the cost of exclusive compute capacity, re-proven periodically by a unique private-key challenge-response. Shared hardware fails verification, so attackers must buy and run separate resources for every fake identity, spending real capital and time while facing slash risk if interaction-graph clustering is detected. Bonds rest on a mesa of ledger checkpoints; juniper-rooted key hierarchies block reuse, and shale-layered commitment proofs raise the barrier each epoch.
